plotSections.title: The Journal and Gerk's Possible Importance
bullets: While the council of gods remains assembled, Sylan publicly reveals to Plymouth Gawater and the others why he believes Gerk is a uniquely important individual.

Sylan explains that years ago he found a handwritten journal containing two notable pieces of information: a search by the Navi for a child whose mother died while the child survived, and a plot against Sylan's family that later came to pass.

Following a spiritual experience in Jotunheim, Sylan became convinced that the child referenced in the journal is Gerk and believes Gerk is destined to act as a Keeper capable of opening the doors tied to the Keystones.
Plymouth carefully questions the source of Sylan's information, focusing on the journal's authorship, age, historical references, and whether it contains prophecy.
Plymouth recognizes the journal by reputation rather than by having personally read it and introduces the previously unknown concept of 'Mother's Prayer,' implying the journal may be connected to it.

chronologicalEvents: The council resumes after the previous session's discussions.
The DM reiterates that councils of gods can last effectively forever from a mortal perspective because time has little meaning to the assembled deities.
The party observes the council: Juten Prime silently listens, Plymouth Gawater contemplates questions, and the other NPCs remain present.
Gerk asks Sylan to explain why Sylan believes Gerk is special.
Sylan tells the assembled group about the journal he discovered years earlier.
Sylan explains the journal described the Navi searching for a child whose mother died while the child survived.
Sylan explains that a later spiritual experience in Jotunheim convinced him that the child is Gerk.
Sylan states his belief that Gerk is a Keeper who will open the doors.
Kit Anger becomes noticeably attentive after hearing the discussion.
Plymouth questions Sylan about the journal's origin, authorship, age, and whether it contains prophecy.
Sylan explains the journal appeared handwritten by multiple authors and accurately predicted the plot that killed his family.
Plymouth says he knows of the journal's existence and asks whether Sylan has heard of something called 'Mother's Prayer.'

notes: Sylan publicly identifies Gerk as the child referenced in an old journal.
Sylan believes Gerk is destined to become a Keeper capable of opening the doors associated with the Keystones.
